reconstructed_theorem_text: For every pair of measurable spaces A and B, every probability measure mu on A, every pair of Markov probability kernels K and L from A to B, and every function epsilon : A -> R integrable with respect to mu, the following implication holds. Suppose that for mu-almost every x in A, simultaneously for every measurable set s in B, |K(x,s) - L(x,s)| <= epsilon(x). Then for every measurable set t in B, |(K_*mu)(t) - (L_*mu)(t)| <= integral_A epsilon(x) mu(dx), where (K_*mu)(t) = integral_A K(x,t) mu(dx) and likewise for L. Here all displayed event masses are their real values, which agree exactly with the finite masses of these probability measures. The exceptional mu-null set in the hypothesis is common to all measurable s. No separate pointwise nonnegativity assumption on epsilon is imposed.
objects: Measurable spaces A and B; a probability measure mu on A; Markov kernels K and L from A to B; an integrable real budget epsilon on A; the two output probability measures K_*mu and L_*mu; measurable events s and t in B.
domains: A and B are arbitrary measurable spaces. mu is a probability measure on A. For each x in A, K(x,.) and L(x,.) are probability measures on B, and each measurable-event mass is measurable as a function of x. epsilon : A -> R is integrable under mu. The conclusion compares real-valued masses of measurable subsets of B.
quantifiers: Universally quantified over A, B, mu, K, L, and epsilon satisfying the assumptions. The hypothesis has the order: for mu-almost every x, for every measurable s in B, the discrepancy is at most epsilon(x). The conclusion holds for every measurable t in B.
assumptions: mu is a probability measure; K and L are Markov probability kernels; epsilon is integrable under mu; and |K(x,s)-L(x,s)| <= epsilon(x) simultaneously for all measurable s at mu-almost every x.
conclusion: For every measurable t in B, |(K_*mu)(t)-(L_*mu)(t)| <= integral_A epsilon dmu, with each output event mass equal to the integral of the corresponding conditional event mass.
scopes: One common mu-null exceptional set suffices for all measurable s in the hypothesis. The kernels, input measure, and budget are fixed while the output event t varies. Event masses are their finite real values. epsilon may depend on x; global pointwise nonnegativity is not an extra hypothesis, although the event bound implies nonnegativity mu-almost everywhere. No restriction to finitely many events or special measurable spaces is stated.
constant_dependencies: The multiplicative constant is exactly 1. The bound depends on mu and epsilon only through integral_A epsilon dmu; it contains no event-dependent constant or factor 2.
